summary: Mitchell G. Weiss is an Indologist who studied under Ludo Rocher. He has served as a professor at the University of Basel.
Mithilesh Chaturvedi works in Indology and linguistics. He was affiliated with the Department of Sanskrit at the University of Delhi, where he is attested as professor emeritus in 2026.

Mitsuji Fukunaga (1918–2001) was a scholar of sinology and philosophy who studied at Hiroshima Higher Normal School and Kyoto University. He taught at Kyoto University (1961–1982), the University of Tokyo (1974–1979), Kansai University, and the University of Kitakyushu.

Mitsukuni Yoshida (1921–1991) was a scholar of Japanese studies, history, and archaeology. He studied at Kyoto University from around 1942 to 1945 and held a post at Kyoto University of the Arts from circa 1986 to 1991.
Mitsunobu Nakasone is a Buddhist studies scholar. He held teaching posts as a part-time lecturer at Bukkyo University (attested 2005) and at Kyoto Bunkyo Junior College (attested 2020).
Mitsutoshi Moriguchi (born 1944) is a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies. He completed doctoral studies at Taisho University, where he also served as a lecturer (attested 1989–1995).
Mitsuyo Demoto is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology. She studied at Kyoto University and holds a post at the University of Marburg, attested in 2024.

Mitsuyoshi Saegusa (1923–2010) was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. He studied at the University of Tokyo, the University of Munich, and Kokugakuin University, later holding professorships at the University of Tsukuba and Nihon University.

Mitsuyuki Ishida (1911–1991) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Ryukoku University from 1931 to 1934. He later served on the faculty at Ryukoku University, including as professor (c. 1958–1980), and at Shitennoji University.
Miyako Notake is a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. She has served as a part-time lecturer at Waseda University, attested in 2015 and 2026.

Mizuho Okita (born 1977) specializes in religious studies and Indology. She earned a BA from Tokai University, studied under Atsuhiko Yoshida and Katsuhiko Kamimura at Gakushuin University, and was a part-time lecturer at Meisei University (attested 2008).
Mizumaro Ishida (1916–1995) was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Japanology. He served as a professor at Tokai University, attested in 1976 and 1987.
Mohammad Ashraf Dar works in history, archaeology, and Indology. He earned an MPhil from Vikram University, where he was also attested as a research scholar in 2014.

Mohammad Habib (1895–1971) was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at Aligarh Muslim University, the University of Allahabad, and New College, Oxford, and later taught Saiyid Athar Abbas Rizvi.

Mokurai Shimaji (1838–1911) was a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who studied under Chō Sanshū. He served as council member at Nishi Hongan-ji, head priest at Gankyo-ji (1892–1905), and founded Chiyoda Jogakuen.

Mona Schrempf is a scholar of Tibetology and religious studies who completed a doctorate at the Free University of Berlin in 2001. In 2006, she was attested as a fellow at Humboldt University and a teacher at Heidelberg University.

Monica Esposito (1962–2011) was a sinologist and religious studies scholar who earned her PhD from Paris Diderot University. She completed post-doctoral studies in Europe and Japan, later serving as an associate professor at Kyoto University (c. 2003–2011).

Monica L. Smith is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology who studied at the University of Michigan. She taught at the University of Pittsburgh (2000–2002) before joining the University of California, Los Angeles as a professor in 2002.

Monier Monier-Williams (1819–1899) was an Indologist and linguist who studied at the University of Oxford under Horace Hayman Wilson. He taught at East India Company College and served as Boden Professor of Sanskrit at Oxford from 1860 to 1887.

Monika Boehm-Tettelbach (born 1941) is an Indologist who completed her doctorate at the Free University of Berlin under Heinz-Jürgen Pinnow and habilitated at Bonn. She held professorships at Cologne, Bamberg, and Heidelberg (1990–2006).
